_comment: CROSS-PROCESS CONTRACT: where cached Potree octrees live on disk.
The Python backend WRITES them (_octree_cache_root in backend-api/main.py);
the Electron main process READS them back through the app:// protocol
silently disagreed on Windows and Linux, so every import produced an octree
the renderer could never fetch and nothing rendered (GitHub issue #4).
This file is the single written-down truth both sides are tested against:
Change one implementation without changing this file and its own test
fails; change this file without changing both implementations and BOTH
tests fail. It is test-only data - neither implementation reads it at
runtime, so a packaged build cannot break on a missing/renamed asset.
Resolution rule, applied identically by both tests:
base = env[baseEnv] if baseEnv is set and non-empty, else join(home, *baseHomeSegments)
PHYTOGRAPH_OCTREE_CACHE_ROOT overrides the whole thing on both sides.
